history.summary: IMPORTANT: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - treat it accordingly in the dataset. Sri Harmandir Sahib (the Golden Temple) is the holiest shrine of Sikhism, founded by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das, who excavated the Amrit Sarovar (Pool of Nectar) in 1577 and founded Amritsar. The temple was designed and built by the fifth Guru, Guru Arjan Dev; its foundation was laid in 1588 by the Muslim Sufi saint Mian Mir, and in 1604 Guru Arjan installed the Adi Granth (later the Guru Granth Sahib), which is recited continuously. Guru Hargobind added the Akal Takht (1606), one of the five seats of Sikh authority. The shrine was destroyed by Afghan invaders under Ahmed Shah Abdali in 1762 and rebuilt; Maharaja Ranjit Singh rebuilt it in marble and copper (1809) and overlaid the sanctum with gold leaf (1830), giving it its name. It was damaged during Operation Blue Star (1984) and subsequently repaired. The langar (community kitchen) serves over 100,000 people daily without discrimination. The complex is on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list. Architecture blends Hindu and Islamic styles; four doors symbolise openness to all faiths and castes.

name: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)
town_description: Amritsar, founded by Guru Ram Das in 1577, is the spiritual and cultural centre of Sikhism in Punjab. The Harmandir Sahib complex, ringed by the Amrit Sarovar and the marble parikrama, anchors the old city. Other key sites: the Akal Takht, Jallianwala Bagh memorial, and the Partition Museum. The city is also famous for its langars and Punjabi cuisine.
